claims.text: In-situ high-resolution transmission electron microscopy with a heating stage can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at atomic resolution.
Nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will retain an ordered atomic structure at elevated temperatures.
The proposed retention of atomic order is caused by entropy stabilization.
The initial equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are crystalline at room temperature.
A controlled in-situ TEM heating protocol can be combined with continuous atomic-resolution imaging.
The experiment will increase temperature gradually from room temperature to a high-temperature application regime under high vacuum or an inert atmosphere.
Nearly equiatomic mixing of five metals creates high configurational entropy.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the AuCoCuNiPt lattice at high temperature.
High configurational entropy suppresses atomic diffusion in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy suppresses disordering transitions in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Suppressing atomic diffusion and disordering transitions prevents structural degradation at high temperature.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will maintain coherent atomic lattice images with minimal sintering or phase separation up to an unspecified high-temperature threshold.
Non-high-entropy or lower-entropy nanoparticles will exhibit atomic rearrangement or diffusion at lower temperatures than AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Room-temperature lattice images provide a baseline for assessing thermally induced structural changes.
Potential electron-beam effects may influence the observed structural behavior.
A lower-entropy nanoparticle control can distinguish entropy stabilization from thermal changes not specific to the high-entropy composition.
